title: A Deep Dive into the OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) | Better Stack Community
snippet: OTLP serves as the protocol for transmitting telemetry data across the OpenTelemetry ecosystem, integrating with instrumentation libraries, SDKs, the OpenTelemetry Collector, and observability backends, facilitating a standardized and flexible observability pipeline.
claim: OTLP is the standardized protocol for transmitting traces, metrics, and logs across the OpenTelemetry ecosystem.

title: GitHub - open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai · GitHub
snippet: OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions cover spans, metrics, and events for GenAI clients, MCP (Model Context Protocol), and provider-specific conventions. These conventions define a standard schema for describing AI and LLM telemetry, backed by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF).
claim: GenAI semantic conventions standardize telemetry attributes for LLM calls, agent steps, and tool use under the gen_ai.* namespace.

title: LLM Observability & Application Tracing (Open Source) - Langfuse
snippet: Langfuse is an open source AI engineering platform providing LLM evals, observability, metrics, prompt management, playground, and datasets. The quickest path to start tracing with Langfuse is the new OTEL-native Langfuse SDK v4, which is a thin layer on top of the official OpenTelemetry client.
claim: Langfuse provides OTLP-native observability for LLM applications through an OpenTelemetry SDK wrapper.

title: OpenTelemetry for LLM tracing: a guide to instrumenting agents and routing spans anywhere - Articles - Braintrust
snippet: You can point your OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT at Phoenix or Langfuse and the same instrumentation keeps working. Rather than sending traces directly from agents to Langfuse or Braintrust, teams can deploy an Open Telemetry Collector on Cloud Run.
claim: OTLP Collectors enable flexible routing of telemetry to multiple backends like Phoenix, Braintrust, and Langfuse.

title: AI Agent Observability - Evolving Standards and Best Practices | OpenTelemetry
snippet: OpenTelemetry is now the observability standard in 2026. As of March 2026, most GenAI semantic conventions are in experimental status, meaning the API isn't fully stabilized yet. However, major observability vendors have already started supporting it.
claim: OpenTelemetry has become the industry standard for AI observability with vendor support from Datadog, Grafana, and others.

query: telemetry metrics traces logs unified observability
title: The 3 pillars of observability: Unified logs, metrics, and traces | Elastic Blog
snippet: Three telemetry signals are the foundational pillars of observability: metrics, logs, and traces. Each serves a distinct purpose. Metrics are the raw numeric data collected from various sources, logs are timestamped messages emitted by services, and distributed tracing lets you observe requests as they propagate through complex systems.
claim: Modern observability requires unified collection of three signals: metrics, logs, and distributed traces.
